sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Everett, WA?
sections.html:
Everett is the Snohomish County seat, and a sale here runs through county offices for excise tax and property tax, plus the city for any permit questions. The city sits about 25 miles north of Seattle on the Port Gardner Peninsula, where the Snohomish River meets Possession Sound. The Census Bureau estimates 113,567 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 110,629 at the 2020 census.

Everett is a renter-heavy market. Only 49.0 percent of homes are owner-occupied, so a good share of sellers are landlords, heirs who inherited a rental, or owners of a house with a basement or backyard unit. That mix shapes which sale route fits: a vacant inherited house, a tenant-occupied duplex and a move-in-ready home on Rucker Hill each call for a different plan.

Everett's economy and layout explain much of the buyer demand. Boeing built its assembly plant at Paine Field in 1967, and Naval Station Everett has operated since 1994. Interstate 5 runs through the city, with US 2 heading to Stevens Pass and State Routes 526, 527 and 529 connecting neighborhoods. Everett Station serves Sounder commuter trains, Amtrak and buses, which matters to anyone commuting to Seattle.

sections.h2: What do Everett housing numbers look like?
sections.html:
Owner-occupied homes in Everett have a median value of $565,300, and 49.0 percent of housing is owner-occupied, per Census Bureau QuickFacts. Values marked 2020-2024 come from the five-year American Community Survey.

sections.h2: Which Everett neighborhoods and local conditions affect a sale?
sections.html:
Everett has 19 recognized neighborhood associations, and buyers shop by area. A few that come up often:

  • Bayside and Port Gardner: downtown, the waterfront and the historic Rucker Hill residential area.
  • Northwest Everett and Riverside: older homes near Everett Community College, with historic districts in both.
  • Lowell: southeast of downtown and once its own town, founded in 1863.
  • Silver Lake, Cascade View and Twin Creeks: south Everett, near Everett Mall and the lake.
  • Westmont: a mostly multifamily area in the southwest.

Most of the city belongs to Everett Public Schools. The southern and western neighborhoods are in the Mukilteo School District, so confirm the district for the address before you describe schools in a listing.

The southwestern neighborhoods include creek ravines that drain to Port Gardner Bay, and the area is prone to mudslides. The city averages about 35.71 inches of rain a year, mostly from October through March. If your lot sits on a slope or near a ravine, collect drainage and retaining wall records before buyers ask.

sections.h2: Can I sell an Everett house that has an accessory dwelling unit?
sections.html:
Yes, and Everett has loosened its rules. Under the city's ADU page, accessory dwelling units are allowed in every zone except Light Industrial and Heavy Industrial, and an ADU is defined as a unit under 1,000 square feet that is subordinate to the main home. The city allows up to two ADUs on a lot. Dwellings under 1,200 square feet need no off-street car parking.

Fee treatment matters to the next owner: transportation impact fees are waived for one added ADU, school impact fees are waived for ADUs, and park impact fees are cut by half. In June 2026 the city also launched a gallery of pre-approved ADU designs, with a licensing fee of about $1,500.

  • If the unit was built without a permit, ask Everett Permit Services at PermitServices@everettwa.gov what is needed to legalize it before you list.
  • The city counts basements and attics as ADU space, though not garages, and each separate dwelling unit needs its own utilities.
  • In a historic overlay, any ADU that is not entirely inside the existing home goes to the Historical Commission.

sections.h2: What are my choices if I need to sell fast in Everett?
sections.html:
Everett sellers usually pick among three routes, and the right one depends on the house and the deadline.

  • List with an agent: the widest buyer pool, with showings, inspections and financing contingencies that add weeks.
  • Sell directly to an investor or cash buyer: fewer contingencies and a closing date you can often choose, usually at a price below a fully prepared listing.
  • Sell it yourself: saves a listing commission, but you handle disclosure forms, pricing and negotiation.

Whichever route you take, ask for the buyer's proof of funds, read the purchase agreement before signing and compare any offer to what you would net after taxes, liens and any loan payoff. A written offer from an escrow company's closing officer shows the figures line by line.

sections.h2: What taxes and paperwork apply when an Everett house sells?
sections.html:
Washington charges a real estate excise tax on each sale, and the Department of Revenue says the seller usually pays it. The state portion is graduated under RCW 82.45.060: 1.1 percent of the first $525,000 of the price, 1.28 percent on the portion up to $1,525,000, 2.75 percent up to $3,025,000 and 3 percent above that. For sales beginning January 1, 2027 the first tier ends at $551,000. A local rate is added on top, so get the combined figure from the Snohomish County Treasurer or your escrow officer.

For a deeded transfer, the excise tax affidavit, the conveyance document and payment go to the county treasurer. The Snohomish County Treasurer lists an excise tax counter open Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., and the office address is 3000 Rockefeller, Everett, WA 98201.

On the property tax side, Snohomish County bills in two halves: April 30 and October 31. Mail payments must be postmarked by the due date. The October 31, 2026 deadline has passed, so any unpaid second-half amount now carries interest and has to be cleared at closing. The next first-half deadline is April 30, 2027.

sections.h2: What happens if I am behind on Everett property taxes?
sections.html:
Late payments carry interest. Under RCW 84.56.020, residential property with four or fewer units is charged 9 percent a year on delinquent taxes, with no added penalties, while larger or nonresidential property faces 12 percent plus penalties. Snohomish County assesses the charge on the first day of each month, and missing the April 30 first-half payment makes the full year's tax delinquent.

The county also warns that a property can go to foreclosure once the third delinquent year's taxes are owed in full. Its Tax Lien Foreclosure Sale is run online, with the list of properties filed in court each May. If you are close to that point, a sale can pay the back taxes out of the proceeds at closing. The Treasurer's page also points to a statute that allows interest and penalties to be waived in limited situations, so ask the office whether you qualify.

faqs.q: How many people live in Everett, WA?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 113,567 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 110,629. Everett is the most populous city in Snohomish County.

faqs.q: Who pays the real estate excise tax when an Everett house sells?
faqs.a: The seller usually pays, according to the Washington Department of Revenue. If the seller does not pay, the buyer becomes responsible, and unpaid tax can become a lien on the property. The state tiers are in RCW 82.45.060, and a local rate is added.

faqs.q: Are accessory dwelling units allowed in Everett?
faqs.a: Yes. ADUs are allowed in every zone except Light Industrial and Heavy Industrial, with up to two per lot and a size cap of 1,000 square feet under the city's definition. Check the permit history of any existing unit before you sell.

faqs.q: When are Snohomish County property taxes due?
faqs.a: First-half or full payment is due April 30, and the second half is due October 31. Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date. The October 31, 2026 date has already passed.

faqs.q: Which school district serves my Everett house?
faqs.a: Most of Everett is in Everett Public Schools, while the southern and western neighborhoods are served by the Mukilteo School District. Confirm the district for your exact address with the district or the county before you advertise schools.
